%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] An effect that creates distortions on the helmet glass. A textured helmet will work independently of this option.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Motion blur - blurring of the image when turning the camera, playing motion scenes, or with fast-moving objects.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the factor by which the maximum visibility distance set in the current weather profile is multiplied. The range of this value is from 0.4 (slider minimum) to 1.5 (slider maximum). For example, the weather has a view distance of 150 meters set. At the slider's minimum you will see 60 meters, at maximum 225. ATTENTION! High view distance can greatly reduce performance on older PCs.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the detail of rendering and lighting of human, monster, and weapon models in the game. The further the slider, the more detailed they will be.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] This setting regulates how densely the tufts of grass are rendered in the game. The further the slider, the closer together the grass elements will be rendered and the thicker it will be. ATTENTION! Excessive grass density leads to severe slowdowns; if you want to adjust this parameter, do so little by little, checking the result each time.

%c[yellow]Default: 100 m.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the maximum distance at which grass is rendered. The further the slider, the further the edge of the grass will be. The slider allows adjusting the distance in the range from 48 (standard distance) to 240 meters. ATTENTION! The game's grass rendering algorithm is such that increasing the grass radius increases the load on the video card exponentially. More or less acceptable values lie within 150-200 meters (middle of the slider).
This setting allows you to enable an optimized grass rendering mode by 'thinning' it at long distances. It allows you to gain a few fps at high values of draw distance and grass density.

This setting regulates the degree of texture detail rendered by the game. The further the slider, the more distinct the textures and the more video memory they require. When lowering this setting, textures will become blurred but, correspondingly, consume less memory.

This setting regulates the degree of anisotropic texture filtering. The minimum slider value corresponds to single filtering, the maximum - sixteenfold. The higher it is, the sharper textures will look as the distance to them increases.
This setting enables marks from bullet impacts on bodies.
This setting enables objects casting shadows from sunlight. On weak PCs, disabling this setting can give a serious speed boost.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting enables grass casting shadows from sunlight and other dynamic light sources. This setting now works - we fixed it. ATTENTION! The setting absolutely WRECKS performance. Do not use it with a large grass draw radius or high grass density!

This setting regulates the preservation of lighting calculation accuracy as the distance to them increases. The higher it is, the more detailed shadows from dynamic light sources will look at a distance.

This setting allows the game to process the volumetric light of NPC flashlights as dynamic light sources. On weak PCs, disabling this setting can give a serious speed boost at night, in camps with a large number of NPCs.
This setting regulates the quality of shadow rendering in the game. The higher it is, the smoother the shadow edges will be.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting allows you to enable vertical synchronization, i.e. synchronization of the frame rate with the monitor's refresh rate. When enabled, the effect of slight horizontal displacement of parts of the screen during sharp mouse movements will disappear, but performance may decrease slightly.

This setting forces the game to always use a video mode with a 60 Hz screen refresh rate. The setting is useful for owners of monitors where the game incorrectly detects the screen refresh rate on startup. However, it is recommended to enable this setting only if you have such a problem. In some rare cases, enabling this setting can cause lags in fullscreen mode.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.
%c[default] This setting switches the anti-aliasing type. Available are NVIDIA DLSS (Deep learning super sampling), AMD FSR2 (FidelityFX Super Resolution), TAA (Temporal anti-aliasing), SMAA (Subpixel Morphological AntiAliasing). 
 
NVIDIA DLSS (anti-aliasing with deep learning algorithms) is a revolutionary AI-based rendering technology that improves graphics quality through the use of specialized tensor cores in GeForce RTX video cards. In desktop and mobile video cards, the technology became available with the arrival of the RTX20 series. Anti-aliasing using DLSS gives a result superior in quality to MSAA 8x, while not causing performance drops. 
 
FSR is a less demanding and lower-quality analog from AMD. FSR 2.0 is supported by all AMD video cards from the RX 400 series and newer, as well as NVIDIA video cards from the 1000 series.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Adjusts post-processing sharpness after anti-aliasing.

This setting regulates the degree of light reflection by shiny and matte surfaces such as metal, leather, wood, etc. ATTENTION! This is a setting in the \"for enthusiasts\" category, and if you don't know exactly what you're doing - leave it at the default value. The further the slider, the stronger the reflection effect, but don't overdo it - at high values surfaces start to look as if wrapped in plastic.

This setting regulates the distance up to which dynamic shadows are rendered in full quality. Beyond this distance they begin to smear and their rendering quality drops, as the shadow calculation switches to a simplified mode. The slider regulates the value in the range from 1 to 60 meters. The parameter should be tuned together with the shadow resolution (in the configurator). The higher you set the slider, the higher you should set the shadow map resolution for good quality.

This setting regulates the field of view within which shadows are rendered normally. If this angle is insufficient, extra triangular shadows will constantly be visible at the edges of the screen. It is recommended to keep the setting at maximum.
Enables the parallax effect on terrain with puddles in the depressions.

This setting enables the HDR Tone mapping effect. It improves the image by accentuating its details, which without this effect would be insufficiently contrasted - small elements, edges - while not making the image excessively bright.

This setting regulates the intensity of the HDR Tone mapping effect. ATTENTION! This is a setting in the \"for enthusiasts\" category, and if you don't know exactly what you're doing - leave it at the default value. Adjust in small steps, since at excessive values of this setting the image becomes surreal and the lit areas become overexposed. Cranking it too high, you'll get an HDR effect reminiscent of Fallout 3.
This setting regulates the intensity of sun lighting. The higher it is, the brighter the sunlit areas will be and the deeper the shadows.

This setting regulates the intensity of diffuse light independent of the sun. The higher it is, the brighter all shaded areas in the game will be, and the paler shadows from the sun will look. ATTENTION! This is a setting in the \"for enthusiasts\" category, and if you don't know exactly what you're doing - leave it at the default value. Increase it if the game as a whole seems too dark to you and you can't achieve the desired effect with the brightness/contrast sliders. It's not recommended to crank it too much - the image will lose depth and start to look flatter.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting switches the type of sun shafts. Choose the one you like more.

This setting enables the effect of softening the edge of water surfaces. With it enabled, water at the edge of bodies of water will smoothly gain transparency up to complete invisibility, which allows you to eliminate the effect of a sharp and strongly noticeable boundary between water and land.

This setting enables the soft particles effect. With it enabled, the appearance of effects such as fire, smoke, explosions, sparks, etc. will be greatly improved. It is recommended to always keep this setting enabled.
This setting regulates the effect of softening shadow edges in the game; with it, shadows look more realistic.
This setting regulates the effect of softening lamp shadows with distance from the lamp. Shadows look more realistic.

This setting enables precomputed global illumination in the game. It uses ready-made hemi lightmaps that allow bringing the picture closer to photorealism. When this setting is enabled, building interiors will become noticeably darker. The setting does not affect performance, since the effect is computed in advance; however, keep in mind that the precomputed and dynamic global illumination effects - r2_ssao - overlay each other. Accordingly, if you want to use both effects, it makes sense to lower the strength of both so as not to get an overly dark picture. Or, if performance is important to you, use only precomputed lighting and disable dynamic global illumination.
This setting regulates the intensity of precomputed global illumination in the game. Higher values allow you to get a more realistic picture but lead to darkening of the scene.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the AO quality in the game. This effect, when enabled, calculates areas additionally shaded by model geometry, making the lighting more similar to lighting in the real world; half-shadows and shading from equipment elements, clothing, vehicle details, grass, and other small parts of geometry appear on models.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the operating mode of the global illumination effect in the game. Available for selection are GTAO (Ground Truth-based Ambient Occlusion) and SSDO (ScreenSpace Directional Occlusion)

%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the enhanced surface relief effect using the Steep parallax mapping algorithm. This algorithm uses ray tracing in heightmap space to calculate relief, which gives a more realistic and higher-quality effect.
This setting enables a component of the depth of field effect - real-time eye focus. It irritates some people, so we left the option to disable it.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting enables a component of the depth of field effect - eye focus on the weapon during reload.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] This setting enables a component of the depth of field effect - blurring of the screen edges when aiming.
This setting regulates the quality of the depth of field effect.
This setting enables Detail relief - displaying small details and roughness on objects.
The setting enables a simulation of 'dirt' on the camera's lens.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting enables the appearance of drops on the glass of helmets and gas masks during rain.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The setting enables wetting of surfaces during rain.
The setting enables volumetric light for some lamps.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The setting enables puddles and reflections in them during rain.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Tessellation increases the quality of low-poly models of NPCs, monsters, the actor's hands, animated items (bottles, etc.). Angular models become more smoothed. %c[red] \nATTENTION! With the current actor hand models, this setting affects FPS!
The setting enables shader optimization mode. It allows raising FPS on video cards with a narrow bus or low memory bandwidth.

The setting allows you to adjust image sharpness. ATTENTION! This is a setting in the \"for enthusiasts\" category, and NORMALLY SHOULD BE DISABLED. Enable it ONLY if you're a fan of a grainy picture. At high values it gives a noticeable halo around objects.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] The setting enables volumetric fog technology. It is used to simulate murky water, haze in low-lying areas, and similar effects.
Adjusts the sun's effective range. With this setting you can gain a bit of FPS in sunny weather. You can reduce it, for example, by half. The picture won't change much, but FPS will be higher.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] The higher the shadow map resolution - the sharper the shadows will be in the distance (more than ~15-20 meters from the protagonist - beyond the boundary of the near shadow cascade). To avoid a noticeable degradation of shadow quality at this boundary, it is recommended to set the resolution no lower than 4096x4096. The setting very strongly affects performance.
Activates simultaneous loading of textures by multiple threads. May slightly reduce save loading time if you have an SSD.
%c[yellow]Default: 67.5.\n%c[default] It makes sense to increase the field of view for wide monitors and depending on individual preferences.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.70.\n%c[default] The player's field of view. If the value is, for example, 0.45 or less (less than the middle of the slider), then the weapon will be closer; if the value is 0.65 or more (more than the middle of the slider), then the weapon will appear further away during play. It makes sense to tune individually for wide monitors and depending on FOV.\n%c[red]For correct weapon display in this mod, a value of 0.70 is recommended.

This setting regulates the intensity of hemi lighting. The higher it is, the brighter it will be. ATTENTION! This is a setting in the \"for enthusiasts\" category, and if you don't know exactly what you're doing - leave it at the default value. Increase it if the game as a whole seems too dark to you and you can't achieve the desired effect with the brightness/contrast sliders.

This setting regulates which frame in sequence will be rendered into the 3D scope. By default - every second one. If you increase it - the FPS in the game will rise, but the FPS in the 3D scope will drop.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.
%c[default] If DLSS or FSR is enabled, this setting regulates the scaling of the image in the 3D scope to improve its clarity. %c[yellow] 
At a value of 1 the image is not scaled. %c[green] 
Optimal value: 2. %c[red] 
At values greater than 2, FPS may drop noticeably.

This setting regulates the rendering distance of dynamic objects, excluding helicopters, crows, and vehicles. The greater the distance - the more objects will be processed by the renderer, and correspondingly FPS may be lower. %c[red] \nIn most cases the default value of 250 meters should be optimal. Increasing it is recommended only if, for some reason, a greater object rendering distance is needed.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Selects the overall game difficulty.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Pauses after loading a save until a key is pressed.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Renders the PDA as a 3D object.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Shows the HUD crosshair. It remains hidden on Master difficulty.

A more forgiving journey through the Zone. You take less damage, find more useful loot, pay less for repairs, recover more effectively, and face reduced mutant ranges and special-ability pressure. Some equipment requirements are also easier to satisfy. %c[yellow]Recommended for first-time players.%c[default]

The intended uncompromising experience. Damage is harsher, useful loot is scarcer, repairs are more expensive, recovery is weaker, and mutants use their full attack ranges and special abilities. Equipment requirements are stricter, and the HUD crosshair is unavailable. %c[yellow]Recommended for NLC veterans.%c[default]
